clinicalDetails.clinicalHistory: Eight months ago, patient was involved in a road traffic accident resulting in a left tibial condylar fracture and an avulsion ACL tear. Open reduction internal fixation was performed by Dr. Hemant Kalyan, followed by 4 to 6 weeks of non-weight bearing and progressive loading. Provisional diagnosis: left tibial condyle fracture, status post-operative 8 months.
clinicalDetails.chiefComplaint: Left knee pain, difficulty performing functional activities, and difficulty walking along with ankle and back pain during prolonged walking following surgery.

subjectiveAssessments.conclusion: Moderate pain with mild irritability particularly during prolonged walking and standing, relieved with rest.

tests.comments: Restricted and painful knee flexion on overpressure

patientAdvice.adviceDetails: Emphasis on restoring extension, improving stability and single leg stability, strengthening quadriceps and functional lower limb musculature, improving ankle mobility, and activating the posterior chain.
